newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Terra Mining recommends Canadian takeover bid.
newsitem.headline: Terra Mining recommends Canadian takeover bid.

text.p: Swedish mining company Terra Mining has recommended shareholders accept a takeover bid by Canadian William Resources Inc for 162.50 crowns ($24.65) a share.
Posting a sharp fall in nine month profits, Terra Mining said its board had appointed CIBC Wood Gundy to advise on the takeover bid that was made on November 2.

"Based among other things on CIBC Wood Gundy's opinion, the board further recommends that Terra Mining's shareholders accept the bid under the condition that financing is guaranteed," the company said in its nine month report.
The bid by William Resources, running from November 14 to December 12, was conditional on the Canadian company acquiring 90 percent of all the shares in Terra Mining.
Terra Mining shares closed at 159 crowns on Friday.
The miner reported a sharp fall in its results after financial items for the nine months ending September 30. It posted a loss of 6.8 million crowns compared to a profit of 13.8 million.
During the period it produced 1,961 kg of gold from its Bjorkdal mine which was a 29 percent increase on the same period a year ago.
The company said it expected to produce a total of 2,700 kg of gold from Bjorkdal in calendar 1996 against 2,217 kg a year ago.
It also produced 177 kg of gold from its new mine Pahtavaara which started production on July 1 this year.
